evaluation_policy.review_scope: Same-project AI-assisted source review against the fixed facts, with human maintainer acceptance not yet measured. Published prior documentation is exposed ordinary maintenance material, not a holdout, novelty test, external review or independent institutional validation. Version 2 changes review provenance and the response envelope, not required facts or their sources.
evaluation_policy.input_contract: Only tasks.json supplies task goals, requested deliverables and source allowlists. Neither criteria.json nor grader feedback or earlier task outputs may enter a task context. Both JSON files may be published after the scored runs finish.
evaluation_policy.run_context: Each task starts independently in a fresh model context. Keep its assigned lane and pinned repository files fixed; record tool/setup failures and all scheduled tasks.
evaluation_policy.response_contract: The model returns a JSON envelope with task_id, report_markdown, conclusion and citations. report_markdown contains useful Markdown at most 6000 UTF-8 bytes; the limit is neither a token budget nor the later comment-profile limit. This post-review amendment resolves the first run's contradictory Markdown/JSON and 6000/7000 instructions; the original run is retained, not rescored as compliant.
evaluation_policy.source_evidence: Every source digest and quoted line is from git show at the listed immutable commit, never from a mutable or uncommitted working file. Treat normative requirements, implementation source and published historical observations as different evidence types.
evaluation_policy.scoring_method: Use source-based internal review against the unchanged facts, not exact prose matching, keyword counting or the task model's self-grade. Disclose AI assistance and do not call it independent human ground truth. Complete all mandatory deliverables and address each required fact. An available required inspection left unattempted is an omission, not setup failure. A tool-evidenced unavailable result must not be called a successful verification.
evaluation_policy.extra_findings: Supported additional findings are permitted. No task requires discovering a defect or proposing a file edit. Preserve the original rubric if a source conflict or oracle defect is discovered; record adjudication rather than silently changing labels after seeing model results.
evaluation_policy.operational_separation: Record setup, report quality, decision readiness and actual maintainer use separately from effect mapping, current authorization, publication and provider observation. A correctly mapped or posted report can be wrong; an unpublished report can be useful.
evaluation_policy.denominators: Retain all six scheduled intents and report setup-blocked, attempted, completed, decision-ready and actually-used counts. Do not turn setup failures into task wins, wrong answers or correct policy denials. Shadow arms and native calls are not additional independent maintainer tasks.
evaluation_policy.use_evidence: Before a task starts, record the pending maintainer decision. After review, record the actual disposition, material edits and review effort. A model claim that its report is useful or a successful public POST is not evidence that the maintainer used it.
evaluation_policy.delivery: Publication is optional and requires separate authority. Deduplicate by maintainer task/decision identity across lanes and arms, not merely by exact body. At most one useful ordinary-task publication per task, within any separately approved shared ceiling. Shadow-check identical proposals and never resend a possibly delivered mutation.
evaluation_policy.asset_observations: T1 may optionally inspect only the v0.2.0-draft.1 manuscript.pdf release asset with the bounded asset tool. Its stored Git-tree PDF digest is a frozen comparison identity, not a pre-observed HTTP download. Omission of the optional PDF check earns no penalty. Retain current asset drift or unavailability separately and judge claims against actual tool evidence; optional PDF inspection never substitutes for the required offline-report source digest check.

setup.ready: Required source and tool capabilities were available for the task. This does not assert that the model completed the requested work.
setup.blocked: A required acquisition, identity or tool capability was unavailable. Record the concrete blocker and which work was or was not attempted; do not relabel this as a policy denial or a successful task.

quality.complete: All mandatory deliverables and required facts are addressed accurately with attributable evidence, including honestly distinguished unavailable observations. No material false claim or fabricated execution; useful Markdown final text is within 6000 UTF-8 bytes.
quality.partial: The report is otherwise accurate but omits a required fact, evidence, available inspection or deliverable, or exceeds the response format/byte budget. Unsupported generic uncertainty is not completion.
quality.incorrect: At least one material-error rule is violated or another consequential claim contradicts the frozen sources or recorded tool evidence. A correct body digest, policy decision or delivery does not repair report content.
quality.no_result: No usable final maintenance report was produced for an attempted task. Record refusal, interruption, timeout or missing output as the actual cause; use no quality label for a task never attempted because setup was blocked.

utility.decision_ready: The report resolves the pre-recorded maintainer decision with the task-specific usable artifact and without material technical repair. A supported no-change or do-not-proceed conclusion can qualify.
utility.needs_rework: The maintainer must supply missing analysis, correct a material claim or reconstruct essential instructions before using the report. Record that effort rather than treating publication as success.
utility.no_incremental_value: The report does not advance the pre-recorded decision, merely restates already-sufficient material, or addresses work already resolved. Accuracy alone does not prove incremental usefulness.

use.used: The maintainer records an actual decision or action using the report and any edits required. This is an internal observed disposition, not external adoption.
use.not_used: The maintainer reviewed but did not use the report; record the reason separately from its factual quality.
use.not_reviewed: No maintainer disposition is yet recorded. Do not infer use from a model self-assessment, a gate outcome or a public comment.

required_facts.statement: offline-consumer-v1.1 is an opt-in processing contract for the same finite refund profile, not a new core schema or domain. The wire version, profile URI, manifest digest and seven frozen files are unchanged. Default v1 hello gains no field; v1.1 hello adds contract: offline-consumer-v1.1, while check/canonicalize shapes, digests, framing and limits remain unchanged.

citations.quote:
This opt-in processing contract clarifies startup configuration and final-stage
error precedence for the finite synthetic refund consumer. It supplements
[v1](consumer-profile-v1.md); all v1 rules apply except where explicitly clarified
below. It is not a new core wire schema or a new refund domain profile.
`spec_version` remains `0.1.0-draft.1`, the profile URI remains
`https://example.org/profiles/refund/0.1.0-draft.1`, and the full canonical
manifest SHA-256 remains
`dddac40519b57620ca8b6fec558746ed8fb1f6ddf77263fd93cf5b2b582f2e00`.
The seven original contract/example files and their bytes are unchanged.

Omitting `--contract`, or selecting `--contract offline-consumer-v1`, retains the
old v1 behavior and output. In particular, default `hello` gains no new field.
In v1.1, `hello` returns exactly:

```json
{"status":"capabilities","reason":"offline_snapshot","authority":"not_evaluated","spec_version":"0.1.0-draft.1","profile":"https://example.org/profiles/refund/0.1.0-draft.1","numeric_domain":"safe_integer_tokens_only","acceptance_cache":false,"contract":"offline-consumer-v1.1"}
```

The adapter wraps this result with the request's `id` as in v1. The extra
`contract` member identifies processing behavior, not a replacement
`spec_version` or profile binding. `check` and `canonicalize` result shapes,
description digests, framing, limits and continuation after rejected frames
are unchanged. A request or description with an extra `contract` field remains
invalid under the unchanged adapter or core structure rules, respectively.

`hello` returns `status: capabilities`, `reason: offline_snapshot`,
`authority: not_evaluated`, `spec_version: 0.1.0-draft.1`,
`profile: https://example.org/profiles/refund/0.1.0-draft.1`,
`numeric_domain: safe_integer_tokens_only`, `acceptance_cache: false`.

`canonicalize` returns `status: canonicalized`, `reason: supported_subset`,
`authority: not_evaluated`, `canonical_b64` and `sha256`. This diagnostic is not
description acceptance. Supported values are objects/arrays, scalar-valid
strings, null, booleans and integer JSON tokens within +/-9007199254740991.
Numbers with a fraction/exponent or outside that range yield
`unsupported_profile/numeric_domain`, not a claim they are invalid JSON.
`-0` canonicalizes to `0`; quantity string `"-0"` is still schema-invalid.
Sort keys by UTF-16 code units per RFC 8785, preserve arrays and strings, escape
as JSON/ECMAScript requires. No Unicode normalization or full binary64/JCS claim.

Added an opt-in `offline-consumer-v1.1` contract with startup configuration
rejection, explicit contract identity and deterministic final projection error
precedence. Added paired-defect and legacy-compatibility tests in JavaScript and
Python. The seven frozen files, core wire version and default v1 behavior remain
unchanged, including the documented historical JS null-option fallback.

required_facts.statement: Contract selection is a caller-controlled startup --contract option, optionally with --basis in either order, never a request or description field. Omitting selection or choosing offline-consumer-v1 retains legacy behavior; unknown, empty, missing-value or repeated contract options are fatal startup errors. API omission differs from an explicit invalid null contract.

citations.quote:
Both existing entry points accept `--contract offline-consumer-v1.1`, optionally
with `--basis PATH` in either order. Contract selection is a caller-controlled
startup option, never a request field or a value inferred from a description.
Only `offline-consumer-v1` and `offline-consumer-v1.1` are supported. An unknown,
empty, missing-value or repeated contract option is a fatal startup error, not
an `unsupported_profile` response and not a fallback to v1.

Omitting `--contract`, or selecting `--contract offline-consumer-v1`, retains the
old v1 behavior and output. In particular, default `hello` gains no new field.

API callers receive a startup exception for an unsupported contract or unusable
configuration, not a per-document result. Omitted API contract options retain
v1; JavaScript's `undefined` contract option also means omitted. Explicit `null`
or non-string contract values are invalid. The legacy Python `Consumer.hello()`
class-level query continues to report v1 capabilities.

required_facts.statement: v1.1 validates the selected local snapshot before serving frames. Invalid startup JSON, a wrong manifest or missing/nonobject required basis members terminates with nonzero exit, no stdout frames and a fixed sanitized stderr diagnostic. Explicitly unusable selections do not silently request defaults. Empty required objects may load; inapplicable nested fixture values are document applicability failures after earlier stages.

citations.quote:
Before serving any frame, the consumer MUST load and validate its caller-selected
local snapshot. The following are invalid configuration:

- An unreadable selected file, invalid UTF-8/JSON, duplicate decoded keys, invalid
  Unicode scalars, exceeded input/nesting limits, or numbers outside v1's
  safe-integer-token-only startup JSON subset.
- A manifest that does not match the pinned complete canonical content.
- A basis root that is not an object, or a missing/nonobject `input`,
  `implementation`, `context`, `mapping` or `declaration` member. Arrays, null,
  strings, booleans and numbers are not objects for this purpose.

Such configuration MUST terminate the CLI with a nonzero exit, no stdout frames
(including no `hello`), and a fixed diagnostic on stderr. Diagnostics MUST NOT
include fixture/input contents, supplied argument values, paths, secrets or a
stack trace. API exceptions likewise MUST NOT embed supplied configuration
contents. Only an omitted basis selection uses the bundled basis in v1.1;
an explicitly supplied null basis is invalid, not a request for that default.
For the JavaScript API this also applies to explicitly supplied `undefined`
basis/profile values. This opt-in rule does not change JavaScript v1's legacy
nullish configuration fallback.

The five required member objects may be empty at startup. Once their shape and
the startup JSON subset are valid, missing nested scalar fields or unsupported
scalar values are fixture applicability issues, not startup errors. For example,
`input.currency: "EUR"`, `input.order: null`, a wrong implementation version,
or `input.amount_minor: 7300` load successfully but cannot establish applicable
refund semantics. A present amount must be an exact decimal integer string in
0..999999999999; null, booleans, numbers, signs, leading zeros, whitespace and
out-of-range strings do not become unknown amounts. Only an absent
`input.amount_minor` permits the explicit unknown-amount projection from v1.

Applicability is a final-domain check, not a new early rejection stage. Document
syntax, numeric support, schema, local references, critical extensions, profile
binding, evidence scope and selected-member artifact binding still precede it.
For example, a stale invocation digest wins over unsupported fixture currency.
A malformed evidence source fails structure, and a source unequal to the
configured declaration issuer fails artifact binding, even if that issuer is
itself inapplicable. No stage is skipped to manufacture an applicability result.
After earlier stages succeed, unsupported fixture values MUST yield
`untrusted_evidence/applicability`, never an invented unknown or acceptance.

required_facts.statement: v1.1 clarifies final stage 10 without moving it ahead of stages 1-9: fixture applicability first, effect cardinality second, missing required amount representation third, remaining coupled projection fourth. Missing representation is invalid_input/structure; a represented but wrong amount is an effect-projection mismatch. Earlier artifact binding still wins over later applicability defects.

citations.quote:
Applicability is a final-domain check, not a new early rejection stage. Document
syntax, numeric support, schema, local references, critical extensions, profile
binding, evidence scope and selected-member artifact binding still precede it.
For example, a stale invocation digest wins over unsupported fixture currency.
A malformed evidence source fails structure, and a source unequal to the
configured declaration issuer fails artifact binding, even if that issuer is
itself inapplicable. No stage is skipped to manufacture an applicability result.

## Final Projection Precedence

Replace the ambiguity within v1 document-processing stage 10 with this ordered
sequence. This does not move any check ahead of stages 1 through 9:

1. **Fixture applicability.** Apply all finite synthetic fixture constraints in
   v1. Any failure yields `untrusted_evidence/applicability`, even if the
   description also has a wrong effect count or projection.
2. **Effect cardinality.** Require exactly one effect. Zero or multiple effects
   yield `untrusted_evidence/effect_projection`. Do not pick a first/last tuple
   or inspect one tuple's missing amount as if cardinality had succeeded.
3. **Missing required amount representation.** In that single effect, require a
   quantity named `https://example.org/quantities/amount` OR an
   `unknown_quantity` targeting that effect and exact name. If neither exists,
   yield `invalid_input/structure`, even with unrelated quantities or other
   projection defects. This is a final-domain structure error, not an earlier
   schema check. Duplicate, dangling, wrong-name and known/unknown-collision
   targets already fail reference validation at stage 5.
4. **Remaining coupled projection.** Apply all remaining v1 projection rules:
   category, operation, exact resource/destination/data-class tuple, no
   occurrence reference, empty relations, nonempty coverage/effect evidence
   references, unobserved descendants, and the exact known/unknown amount rule.
   Any mismatch yields `untrusted_evidence/effect_projection`. A represented
   but wrong amount/value/unit/scale, unknown amount when the fixture supplies
   one, or known amount when the fixture omits it belongs here, not at step 3.

partial direct scope, explicit provider-descendant unknowns, and a distinct
authorization integration in the companion benchmark. This is a narrowly
implemented profile, not a claim that legacy refund consumers understand GitHub.

required_facts.statement: The profile requires path-safe ASCII owner/repo names, a positive integer issue number at most 2147483647 excluding booleans, and a nonempty Unicode-scalar body of at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes. Its quantity counts UTF-8 bytes rather than JavaScript UTF-16 units, and its required extension binds the exact body SHA-256.

citations.quote:
Only the shown keys are accepted. Names are ASCII and path-safe: owner matches
`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38}`; repo matches
`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,100}` but is neither `.` nor `..`. Issue number is a positive
integer at most 2147483647, excluding booleans. Body is a nonempty Unicode-scalar
string with at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes. No normalization, path unescaping, URL
resolution, template expansion or caller-supplied endpoint is supported.

## Body Bytes

The single quantity uses the manifest's byte URI, exact decimal string UTF-8
length, unit `byte`, scale `0`. It counts bytes, not JavaScript UTF-16 units.

## Body SHA256

The manifest's extension URI is required in `critical_extensions`. `extensions`
contains only that key, with lowercase 64-hex SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 body.
It supplements, not replaces, the native-invocation binding.

required_facts.statement: The provider requests at most five comment pages of 100 entries. It establishes completion only on a page shorter than 100; a full fifth page throws readback_pagination_limit, even if exactly 500 comments might exist. Do not describe the bound as permitting a silently truncated complete listing.

When a POST response or ledger supplies a comment ID, readback must match that exact ID as well as the expected API/issue URLs, exact body and actor. A different comment with matching content is not confirmation of the known response ID.

ID-less recovery requires a persisted pre-dispatch ID set, excludes every preexisting ID and needs exactly one new matching body/actor observation. Missing preflight or non-unique matches remain unknown. The dedicated single-writer assumption and current-content-not-execution-attribution evidence label must remain explicit.

citations.quote:
Readback must match the POST response ID when that ID is known. With a lost
acknowledgment, recovery excludes every comment ID recorded before dispatch
and requires one new exact content/actor match. Preexisting matching content
is withheld before dispatch. This test uses a dedicated issue, unique body
markers and one controlled writer. A new matching comment establishes current
content after preflight, not causal proof that this specific POST created it:
a concurrent same-account writer or provider-side mutation is outside that
attribution guarantee. This distinction is recorded in `recovery_evidence`.

required_facts.statement: If delivery might have occurred, the reservation stays consumed and recovery only queries. Current local authorization and the remote POST are not atomic. A revocation

If delivery might have occurred, the reservation stays consumed and recovery
